info.title: distribute.you MCP Service
info.description: MCP (Model Context Protocol) server for distribute.you. Exposes campaign management tools via MCP protocol over HTTP.

distribute_status.description: Check the connection and say who the key belongs to: the user, and every organization the key reaches with its brands. A key belongs to its USER and reaches every organization that user is a member of; it never belongs to a brand. Call this first: the other tools take a brandId (and an orgId when a brand sits in several organizations) from this list. Then, before acting on or answering what the client asks (a question about results, set something up, change how a campaign behaves, launch, attach files, caps...), read the method: distribute_list_skills, then distribute_read_skill on `index` and on every skill whose description matches the ask. They are the steps our own Copilot follows; an API route alone rarely is the whole setup. Before writing anything a person will read (a reply to the client, an email, a message, a file), read `client-comms`: how we speak to clients and prospects. A key that reaches many organizations (a distribute.you staff key reaches all of them) should pass `search` with a name or domain ("acme", "acme.com") to get only the organizations and brands that match. Keys are created and revoked at https://dashboard.distribute.you and sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.

search.description: Only the organizations whose id or name contains this text, or that hold a brand whose id, name or domain contains it (case-insensitive).

distribute_list_skills.description: List the method skills: how to organize a client's request on distribute.you (offers and their documents, the catalogue, sales funnels, campaigns and their caps, triggers, billing, workflows and plays...), the same skills our own Copilot follows. Each skill has a `slug`, a `title`, and a `description` saying when to read it; `parentSlug` places it in the tree (root: `index`). A skill described as "Always loaded" is loaded for our own Copilot only: you read it yourself. Read this BEFORE acting on a client ask, then read `index` and every matching skill with distribute_read_skill, and `client-comms` before writing anything a person will read. Free, read-only, the same for every client: names no brand or organization.

distribute_read_skill.description: Read one method skill in full (markdown `content`): the steps, the API operations to call in order and the traps. Start with `index`, then the skills distribute_list_skills shows matching the client's ask; read `client-comms` before writing anything a person will read. Follow them; run the operations they name with distribute_call_api (distribute_describe_api for their parameters). Free, read-only.

distribute_signup_start.description: No human needed: request a key with an email, prepay when you need to spend. Step 1 of 2 to open a distribute.you account and get an API key, with no key and no dashboard. Give an email you can read and a phone number in international format (+33612345678; only its format is checked). A 6-digit code is emailed; then call distribute_signup_complete with it. An email that already has an account works too: it gets one more key for that account. Free to call. Pay as you go: you prepay a balance when you want to spend (distribute_prepay), and each action is billed at its price on https://distribute.you/catalog.

email.description: Email to open the account with. The code is sent there.

phone.description: Phone number in international format, e.g. +33612345678. Only its format is checked.

distribute_signup_complete.description: Step 2 of 2: send the 6-digit code emailed by distribute_signup_start and get an API key. This MCP session uses the new key at once (when it had none or its key was refused), so every other tool works right after. Keep `apiKey`: it is shown once. To use it later, reconnect this MCP server with the header `Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>`, or call https://api.distribute.you with that header. Each call makes a NEW key. Reading the account is free; anything that spends needs a prepaid balance first (distribute_prepay).

keyName.description: A name for the key, to recognize it later (e.g. the agent's name).

distribute_prepay.description: No human needed: request a key with an email, prepay when you need to spend. Prepay before calls that spend money (a call that needs money and finds none answers 402 payment_required). Returns a payment `url`: open it, or give it to your human to pay by card. The card is saved and reloads the balance automatically: when the balance falls under `auto_topup_threshold_cents`, it adds `auto_topup_amount_cents`. Auto top-up is required. Amounts in cents, minimums: topup_amount_cents 1000 ($10), auto_topup_amount_cents 1500 ($15), auto_topup_threshold_cents 500 ($5). Less is refused with `amount_below_minimum`, naming the field. Pay as you go: each action is billed from the balance at its price on https://distribute.you/catalog (an email sent is priced by its BounceVerify verdict). What a campaign may spend is its own cap, set on the campaign. Then check distribute_prepaid_status until `state` is `active`. Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

topup_amount_cents.description: First prepayment, in cents. At least 1000 ($10).

auto_topup_amount_cents.description: Amount added at each automatic reload, in cents. At least 1500 ($15).

auto_topup_threshold_cents.description: Balance under which the card reloads, in cents. At least 500 ($5).

cancel_url.description: Page shown if payment is cancelled (default https://distribute.you/?prepaid=cancelled).

brandId.description: Brand to act on (from distribute_status). Selects the organization holding it. Required when your key reaches several organizations, unless orgId is given.

orgId.description: Organization to act in (from distribute_status). Add it when a brand sits in several organizations, or to act in an organization without naming a brand.

distribute_prepaid_status.description: Read the prepaid account: `state` (awaiting_payment: not paid yet; active: ready to spend; card_not_reloadable or auto_topup_off: fix it with distribute_prepay; not_prepaid), `balance_cents`, `paid_cents`, the automatic reload settings and whether the saved card can reload. Free to call. Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

distribute_list_workflows.description: List all available workflows. Includes styled workflows written in the style of industry experts (e.g. Hormozi). Which workflow runs on a step is never picked by you or the client: the platform ranks the workflows of each step like a multi-armed bandit (the best return on spend runs, newer ones still get tried until measured). A step that must behave a certain way is a play (distribute_read_skill `catalogue-plays`). Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

human_id.description: Filter by human expert ID (for styled workflows)

brandId.description: Brand to act on (from distribute_status). Selects the organization holding it. Required when your key reaches several organizations, unless orgId is given.

orgId.description: Organization to act in (from distribute_status). Add it when a brand sits in several organizations, or to act in an organization without naming a brand.

distribute_list_campaigns.description: List the campaigns of one brand or organization. A campaign is one sales funnel run for one offer of a brand, started or paused as a whole. Each campaign has a name, a status (`ongoing` = running, `stopped` = paused), a type (`proactive`: it reaches out to new people on its own; `reactive`: it acts when something happens, such as a reply), and its caps: a max budget and/or a max volume per period, in words in `budget` and `volume` ("Max $10/day", "Up to 50 leads handled/week"), with what the current period used in `maxBudget` and `maxVolume`. A campaign with no max budget spends nothing. Report each campaign by its name. Each campaign also says what starts it, in `runsWhen` ("Each time: Email Pushed Via API" for a reactive campaign, with its `trigger` {slug, name}; "On its own, within its caps (no trigger)" for a proactive one), and what it does, in `path` (its steps in order, e.g. "Lead → Sales Cold Email Outreach → Positive reply → Paid client"; the outcome names are the platform's own, read as served). Every trigger a campaign can start on, and which ones you may fire: distribute_list_triggers. Before telling the client something is missing, read the running (`ongoing`) campaigns: one may already do what they ask (e.g. send an email they wrote: a running campaign that runs "Each time: Email Pushed Via API"). Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

brandId.description: Brand to act on (from distribute_status). Selects the organization holding it. Required when your key reaches several organizations, unless orgId is given.

orgId.description: Organization to act in (from distribute_status). Add it when a brand sits in several organizations, or to act in an organization without naming a brand.

status.description: Filter by campaign status: `ongoing` (running) or `stopped`. `all`, or no status, returns every campaign. Any other value is refused.

distribute_campaign_stats.description: Get one campaign's results: pass `campaignId`, the campaign id from distribute_list_campaigns (the older name `campaign_id` still works). A campaign runs as one; its results come in `results`, one entry per outcome it brings in (`outcome`, such as Positive reply or Lead; `bringsIn` is the older name of the same value) with the channel doing it (`channel`). An id seen elsewhere (trigger events, offer stats, a lead's `campaignId`) is one step of a campaign: pass it too, the answer names its campaign in `note`. Report the campaign by its name and never call an entry of `results` a campaign. Report meetings, positive replies and delivery rate first, then volume and cost; bounces and other failures last. Each entry is ordered that way: `headline`, then `summary`, then the raw figures, then `failureDetails`. Show zeros plainly (0 meetings is still reported). Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

campaign_id.description: Older name of `campaignId`, still accepted. Prefer `campaignId`.

Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

distribute_suggest_icp.description: Analyze a brand's website and suggest an Ideal Customer Profile (ICP). Use this when the user doesn't know who to target and wants AI-generated targeting suggestions. Returns a description of the ideal customers to aim a campaign at. Name the brand by brandId, or by brand_url (matched against the brands of the targeted organization). Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

brand_url.description: The brand/company URL to analyze for ICP extraction. Optional when brandId is given.

distribute_list_leads.description: List the leads (prospects, people we found and contacted) of a brand, newest first, with where each one stands: contacted, sent, delivered, clicked, replied (and how the reply was classified), bounced, unsubscribed, with dates. Each lead carries an `id` (this lead on one campaign) to pass to distribute_get_lead for its emails and conversation, and a `leadId` (the person, the id trigger events and emails name; distribute_get_lead takes it too). Pages with `cursor`: pass the `nextCursor` of the previous page. `total` is the brand's lead count. Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

brandId.description: Brand whose leads to list (from distribute_status).

orgId.description: Organization to act in (from distribute_status). Add it when a brand sits in several organizations, or to act in an organization without naming a brand.

campaignId.description: Only leads of this campaign part (a lead's `campaignId`).

distribute_list_emails.description: List the cold emails we wrote and sent for a brand: for each prospect, the first email and every follow-up (`subject`, then `sequence`: one entry per step with its `bodyText`, its `kind` (first_email or follow_up) and its send `status`: `sent` at `sentAt` (it went out and nothing refused it), `bounced` (it went out at `sentAt` but the receiving server refused it at `bouncedAt`: the prospect never got it, never report it as delivered), `queued` (goes out in the prospect's business hours) or `stopped` (will not go out: reply, bounce, opt-out, meeting, sequence stopped)), with who it went to (`leadEmail`, lead name, title, company, `leadId`). Use it to answer "what did you send for my brand, and what is still queued". Replies and delivery are on distribute_list_leads / distribute_get_lead. Pages with `limit` and `offset`. Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

brandId.description: Brand whose emails to list (from distribute_status).

orgId.description: Organization to act in (from distribute_status). Add it when a brand sits in several organizations, or to act in an organization without naming a brand.

campaignId.description: Only the emails of this campaign part.

distribute_get_lead.description: Everything about ONE lead in one call: who they are and where they stand (sent, delivered, replied...), the emails we wrote for them (first email and follow-ups, subject and body, each with its send status: sent at sentAt, bounced (went out at sentAt, refused by the receiving server at bouncedAt: not delivered), queued or stopped), and the conversation (every message we sent and every reply they wrote, oldest first). Pass `leadId`: either a lead's `id` from distribute_list_leads (this lead on one campaign), or the person's id: a list row's `leadId`, or the `ranLeads[].leadId` a trigger event (POST /v1/trigger-events) answers. With the person's id, also pass `campaignId` (the `ranLeads[].campaignId` beside it, or a lead's `campaignId`) or brandId, so the lead is read directly on that campaign (with only a brandId, among the brand's newest 1,000 leads); the answer's `lead.id` is then the lead's `id`. The older name `lead_id` still works. Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

leadId.description: A lead's `id` from distribute_list_leads, or the person's id (a list row's `leadId`, a trigger event's `ranLeads[].leadId`). Required (or `lead_id`).

lead_id.description: Older name of `leadId`, still accepted. Prefer `leadId`.

campaignId.description: With a person's id: the campaign step they are on (`ranLeads[].campaignId` of the trigger event, or a lead's `campaignId`).

brandId.description: Brand to act on (from distribute_status). Selects the organization holding it. Required when your key reaches several organizations, unless orgId is given.

orgId.description: Organization to act in (from distribute_status). Add it when a brand sits in several organizations, or to act in an organization without naming a brand.

distribute_list_triggers.description: List the triggers: the entry doors a reactive campaign starts on, each with its `id`, `name`, what it means, its `type` (`outcome`: an outcome just reached for a person, named by `outcome`; `condition`: computed by us) and `callable`. Outcome triggers (an outcome was just reached for a person: Form submitted, Meeting booked, Paid client...) are callable: fire one when that fact happens in the client's own tools. Condition triggers computed by us (an outcome + a delay + "still not" another, a GitHub issue in prod...) are never fired by a call: report the outcome they wait on instead, they follow from it. Each trigger's `callable` decides: fire only one with `callable: true`. A new outcome or trigger is a feature request to the distribute.you team, never created by a call: file it with distribute_call_api `POST /v1/staff-requests` (distribute_describe_api for its body), naming the event, where it comes from and an example; the `staff-requests` skill says how. To fire a callable one for a person when the fact happens ("a form was submitted by jane@acme.com"): distribute_call_api POST /v1/trigger-events with body {triggerId, brandId, offerId, person: {email, name?}, item?, idempotencyKey?} (the brand's offers: GET /v1/brands/{id}/offers). Every live campaign of that offer starting on the trigger runs for the person, within its caps; the answer's `event.outcome` says `ran` or `skipped` with the reason (`no_campaign`: no campaign starts on it; `campaign_off`: the ones that do are paused). A `callable: false` trigger is refused before the call: tell the user it is computed by us and fires on its own, and offer to report the outcome it `followsFrom` if that really happened. The same for every client: names no brand or organization. Free, read-only.

distribute_find_people.description: Find the people a brand deals with (from Gmail, WhatsApp and other chats, the CRM, Stripe, signups...), one entry per real person, and read how we see each one: `tags` (who they are to the user and to the brand: `personal_to_user` (personal: family or a friend of the user who connected the account), `personal_not_to_user` (personal, but not about that user (someone else's private life)), `professional_to_brand` (work, about this brand: a prospect, client, user or partner), `professional_not_to_brand` (work, about something else: a supplier, the user's other activities, a bank...)) and `companies` (the companies they speak for at work, each with its `companyId` and `domain`). Use it to find the person the user talks about ("Mom", "Jane from Acme", "jane@acme.com", "+33612345678") before correcting anything: `q` matches a name, an email, a phone, a company or words from their messages. Each entry carries the `personId` the correction tools take. A tag or company the user stated themselves says `statedByUser: true`. `scope.status` `building` means the brand's people are still being gathered: ask again in a minute. Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

brandId.description: Brand whose people to search (from distribute_status).

orgId.description: Organization to act in (from distribute_status). Add it when a brand sits in several organizations, or to act in an organization without naming a brand.

q.description: Who to find: a name, an email, a phone (4+ digits), a company or words they wrote. Omit for the most recent people.

distribute_list_people_companies.description: List the companies a brand's people speak for at work, most people first: each with its `companyId`, its `domains`, how many of the brand's people speak for it (`people`) and in what capacity (`tags`: about this brand, or about something else, with how many carry each). Use it for "which companies do my contacts work for?" or to find a company's id before removing it from a person. To see WHO works there, search the people with distribute_find_people (q = the company's domain). Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

brandId.description: Brand whose people's companies to list (from distribute_status).

orgId.description: Organization to act in (from distribute_status). Add it when a brand sits in several organizations, or to act in an organization without naming a brand.

distribute_correct_person.description: Fix how we see a person, or an email domain, when the user says we got it wrong. Only call it when the user asks for the change; say what you are about to change first. One fix per call (`change`): `add_tag` / `remove_tag` with `personId` and `tag` ("Mom is a client of mine, not family" = remove_tag personal_to_user, then add_tag professional_to_brand: two calls); `add_company` with `personId` and the company's `domain` or website ("she works at Acme": acme.com), optionally `tags` for how they speak for it; `remove_company` with `personId` and `companyId` ("she left Acme": the id from the person's `companies`); `domain_is` with `domain` and `domainKind`: `mailbox_provider` (a public mailbox like gmail.com, its users are not one company) or `organization` ("mybiz.co is a company, not a public mailbox"). Tags: `personal_to_user` (personal: family or a friend of the user who connected the account), `personal_not_to_user` (personal, but not about that user (someone else's private life)), `professional_to_brand` (work, about this brand: a prospect, client, user or partner), `professional_not_to_brand` (work, about something else: a supplier, the user's other activities, a bank...). The user's word wins over our automatic reading until undone; a newer fix on the same thing takes back the older one (an add takes back an earlier remove of that tag or company, and the reverse): read distribute_list_people_corrections first to see what the user already stated, removals included (distribute_find_people shows only what a person carries now). It shows on the people within about a minute (re-read with distribute_find_people). The same fix twice answers `duplicate: true`. Keep the returned `correctionId`: "undo that" = distribute_undo_people_correction with it. Refusals come back with their `reason`: `person_not_found` (search again with distribute_find_people), `company_unresolved` (no company is known for that domain: check the spelling or use the website), `tags_required` (say how the person speaks for that company: professional_to_brand and/or professional_not_to_brand), `invalid_correction` (a field is missing for that change). Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

brandId.description: Brand the person belongs to (from distribute_status).

orgId.description: Organization to act in (from distribute_status). Add it when a brand sits in several organizations, or to act in an organization without naming a brand.

personId.description: The person, from distribute_find_people. Every change but `domain_is`.

tag.description: add_tag / remove_tag: the tag to add or remove.

domain.description: add_company: the company's domain or website. domain_is: the email domain (e.g. mybiz.co).

companyId.description: remove_company: the company's `companyId` from the person's `companies`.

tags.description: add_company: how the person speaks for it (professional_to_brand and/or professional_not_to_brand). Default: their own work tags.

reason.description: Why, in the user's words (kept with the fix).

distribute_list_people_corrections.description: List every fix stated on a brand's people, newest first, undone ones included: `corrections` (tags, companies, domain verdicts; each with its `correctionId`, `change`, the person, `reason`, when, and `undoneAt` once taken back) and `merges` (two people stated as one, each with its `mergeId`). Use it for "what did I change?" or to find the fix to take back when the user says "undo that" about an earlier one. Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

brandId.description: Brand whose fixes to list (from distribute_status).

orgId.description: Organization to act in (from distribute_status). Add it when a brand sits in several organizations, or to act in an organization without naming a brand.

distribute_undo_people_correction.description: Take back a fix made with distribute_correct_person, when the user says "undo that" or "put it back": our automatic reading applies again within about a minute. Pass its `correctionId` (from the fix's answer, or distribute_list_people_corrections). A fix made of two calls (remove a tag, add another) is undone with two calls, in any order. Undo goes back to our AUTOMATIC reading, not to an earlier fix this one took back: if the user had stated something before (listed as undone at the moment this fix was made), say so and, when the user wants that back, state it again with distribute_correct_person. The fix stays listed as undone. Undoing twice answers `duplicate: true`; an unknown id is refused `correction_not_found`. Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

brandId.description: Brand the fix was made on (from distribute_status).

orgId.description: Organization to act in (from distribute_status). Add it when a brand sits in several organizations, or to act in an organization without naming a brand.

distribute_merge_people.description: State that two people of a brand are the same human ("these two are the same person": a WhatsApp chat with a number never saved and the same person on Gmail). Only call it when the user says so. Pass both `personIds` from distribute_find_people. They show as one person within about a minute. Keep the returned `mergeId`: "undo that" = distribute_undo_people_merge. Refusals come back with their `reason`: `person_not_found`, `same_person` (both ids are already the same person), `already_one_person`, `different_brand`. Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

brandId.description: Brand both people belong to (from distribute_status).

orgId.description: Organization to act in (from distribute_status). Add it when a brand sits in several organizations, or to act in an organization without naming a brand.

distribute_undo_people_merge.description: Split back two people stated as one with distribute_merge_people ("they are not the same person", "undo that"). Each gets back their own person within about a minute. Pass its `mergeId` (from the merge's answer, or distribute_list_people_corrections). Undoing twice answers `duplicate: true`; an unknown id is refused `merge_not_found`. Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

brandId.description: Brand the merge was made on (from distribute_status).

orgId.description: Organization to act in (from distribute_status). Add it when a brand sits in several organizations, or to act in an organization without naming a brand.

distribute_find_api.description: Find how to do something in distribute.you when no other tool covers it. Searches every operation of the distribute.you API (the same API and the same scope your key has: leads, emails, conversations, campaigns and their caps, offers, sales funnels, triggers, billing, CRM, stats...) by what you want to do, in plain words ("list the emails sent for my brand", "set a campaign's max budget", "pause a campaign", "account balance"). Returns the best matching operations (method, path, summary, required parameters). Then call distribute_describe_api for the details and distribute_call_api to run it. With no query, lists the areas of the API and how many operations each has. To list the triggers (and which ones a call may fire), use distribute_list_triggers.

query.description: What you want to do, in plain words.

area.description: Restrict to one area (as listed with no query), e.g. Leads, Emails, Billing.

distribute_describe_api.description: Read one distribute.you API operation in full before calling it: what it does, its path and query parameters (required or not), the JSON body it takes, and `answers`: what a successful call returns (per status, the JSON shape with each field's meaning), so you can act on the answer. Name it by `operationId`, or by `method` and `path`, as distribute_find_api returned them.

path.description: Path template (/v1/leads/{id}) or a concrete path.

distribute_call_api.description: Call any distribute.you API operation with your key, exactly as the API would answer it (same scope, same refusals). Use it for anything the other tools do not cover; find the operation with distribute_find_api first. `path` is the concrete path with its ids filled in (/v1/leads/123/timeline); query parameters go in `query`, a JSON body in `body`. Writes (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) change the account for real: say what you are about to change before calling. Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

body.description: JSON body for POST, PUT and PATCH.

brandId.description: Brand to act on (from distribute_status). Selects the organization holding it. Required when your key reaches several organizations, unless orgId is given.

orgId.description: Organization to act in (from distribute_status). Add it when a brand sits in several organizations, or to act in an organization without naming a brand.

A key belongs to its USER and reaches every organization that user is a member of; it never belongs to a brand. Before writing anything a person will read (a reply to the client, an email, a message, a file), read `client-comms`: how we speak to clients and prospects. A key that reaches many organizations (a distribute.you staff key reaches all of them) should pass `search` with a name or domain ("acme", "acme.com") to get only the organizations and brands that match. The card is saved and reloads the balance automatically: when the balance falls under `auto_topup_threshold_cents`, it adds `auto_topup_amount_cents`. Auto top-up is required. Amounts in cents, minimums: topup_amount_cents 1000 ($10), auto_topup_amount_cents 1500 ($15), auto_topup_threshold_cents 500 ($5). Less is refused with `amount_below_minimum`, naming the field. post.summary: List the campaigns of one brand or organization. A campaign is one sales funnel run for one offer of a brand, started or paused as a whole. Each campaign has a name, a status (`ongoing` = running, `stopped` = paused), a type (`proactive`: it reaches out to new people on its own; `reactive`: it acts when something happens, such as a reply), and its caps: a max budget and/or a max volume per period, in words in `budget` and `volume` ("Max $10/day", "Up to 50 leads handled/week"), with what the current period used in `maxBudget` and `maxVolume`. A campaign with no max budget spends nothing. Report each campaign by its name. Each campaign also says what starts it, in `runsWhen` ("Each time: Email Pushed Via API" for a reactive campaign, with its `trigger` {slug, name}; "On its own, within its caps (no trigger)" for a proactive one), and what it does, in `path` (its steps in order, e.g. "Lead → Sales Cold Email Outreach → Positive reply → Paid client"; the outcome names are the platform's own, read as served). Every trigger a campaign can start on, and which ones you may fire: distribute_list_triggers. Before telling the client something is missing, read the running (`ongoing`) campaigns: one may already do what they ask (e.g. send an email they wrote: a running campaign that runs "Each time: Email Pushed Via API"). Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

post.summary: List the triggers: the entry doors a reactive campaign starts on, each with its `id`, `name`, what it means, its `type` (`outcome`: an outcome just reached for a person, named by `outcome`; `condition`: computed by us) and `callable`. Outcome triggers (an outcome was just reached for a person: Form submitted, Meeting booked, Paid client...) are callable: fire one when that fact happens in the client's own tools. Condition triggers computed by us (an outcome + a delay + "still not" another, a GitHub issue in prod...) are never fired by a call: report the outcome they wait on instead, they follow from it. Each trigger's `callable` decides: fire only one with `callable: true`. A new outcome or trigger is a feature request to the distribute.you team, never created by a call: file it with distribute_call_api `POST /v1/staff-requests` (distribute_describe_api for its body), naming the event, where it comes from and an example; the `staff-requests` skill says how. To fire a callable one for a person when the fact happens ("a form was submitted by jane@acme.com"): distribute_call_api POST /v1/trigger-events with body {triggerId, brandId, offerId, person: {email, name?}, item?, idempotencyKey?} (the brand's offers: GET /v1/brands/{id}/offers). Every live campaign of that offer starting on the trigger runs for the person, within its caps; the answer's `event.outcome` says `ran` or `skipped` with the reason (`no_campaign`: no campaign starts on it; `campaign_off`: the ones that do are paused). A `callable: false` trigger is refused before the call: tell the user it is computed by us and fires on its own, and offer to report the outcome it `followsFrom` if that really happened. The same for every client: names no brand or organization. Free, read-only.

Use it to find the person the user talks about ("Mom", "Jane from Acme", "jane@acme.com", "+33612345678") before correcting anything: `q` matches a name, an email, a phone, a company or words from their messages. Each entry carries the `personId` the correction tools take. A tag or company the user stated themselves says `statedByUser: true`. `scope.status` `building` means the brand's people are still being gathered: ask again in a minute. post.summary: Fix how we see a person, or an email domain, when the user says we got it wrong. Only call it when the user asks for the change; say what you are about to change first. One fix per call (`change`): `add_tag` / `remove_tag` with `personId` and `tag` ("Mom is a client of mine, not family" = remove_tag personal_to_user, then add_tag professional_to_brand: two calls); `add_company` with `personId` and the company's `domain` or website ("she works at Acme": acme.com), optionally `tags` for how they speak for it; `remove_company` with `personId` and `companyId` ("she left Acme": the id from the person's `companies`); `domain_is` with `domain` and `domainKind`: `mailbox_provider` (a public mailbox like gmail.com, its users are not one company) or `organization` ("mybiz.co is a company, not a public mailbox"). Tags: `personal_to_user` (personal: family or a friend of the user who connected the account), `personal_not_to_user` (personal, but not about that user (someone else's private life)), `professional_to_brand` (work, about this brand: a prospect, client, user or partner), `professional_not_to_brand` (work, about something else: a supplier, the user's other activities, a bank...). The user's word wins over our automatic reading until undone; a newer fix on the same thing takes back the older one (an add takes back an earlier remove of that tag or company, and the reverse): read distribute_list_people_corrections first to see what the user already stated, removals included (distribute_find_people shows only what a person carries now). It shows on the people within about a minute (re-read with distribute_find_people). The same fix twice answers `duplicate: true`. Keep the returned `correctionId`: "undo that" = distribute_undo_people_correction with it. Refusals come back with their `reason`: `person_not_found` (search again with distribute_find_people), `company_unresolved` (no company is known for that domain: check the spelling or use the website), `tags_required` (say how the person speaks for that company: professional_to_brand and/or professional_not_to_brand), `invalid_correction` (a field is missing for that change). Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

post.summary: Find how to do something in distribute.you when no other tool covers it. Searches every operation of the distribute.you API (the same API and the same scope your key has: leads, emails, conversations, campaigns and their caps, offers, sales funnels, triggers, billing, CRM, stats...) by what you want to do, in plain words ("list the emails sent for my brand", "set a campaign's max budget", "pause a campaign", "account balance"). Returns the best matching operations (method, path, summary, required parameters). Then call distribute_describe_api for the details and distribute_call_api to run it. With no query, lists the areas of the API and how many operations each has. To list the triggers (and which ones a call may fire), use distribute_list_triggers.
post.description: MCP Tool: distribute_find_api. Call via JSON-RPC on /mcp with method "tools/call" and params.name="distribute_find_api".

query.description: What you want to do, in plain words.

area.description: Restrict to one area (as listed with no query), e.g. Leads, Emails, Billing.

post.summary: Read one distribute.you API operation in full before calling it: what it does, its path and query parameters (required or not), the JSON body it takes, and `answers`: what a successful call returns (per status, the JSON shape with each field's meaning), so you can act on the answer. Name it by `operationId`, or by `method` and `path`, as distribute_find_api returned them.
post.description: MCP Tool: distribute_describe_api. Call via JSON-RPC on /mcp with method "tools/call" and params.name="distribute_describe_api".

path.description: Path template (/v1/leads/{id}) or a concrete path.

post.summary: Call any distribute.you API operation with your key, exactly as the API would answer it (same scope, same refusals). Use it for anything the other tools do not cover; find the operation with distribute_find_api first. `path` is the concrete path with its ids filled in (/v1/leads/123/timeline); query parameters go in `query`, a JSON body in `body`. Writes (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) change the account for real: say what you are about to change before calling. Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.
post.description: MCP Tool: distribute_call_api. Call via JSON-RPC on /mcp with method "tools/call" and params.name="distribute_call_api".

body.description: JSON body for POST, PUT and PATCH.

brandId.description: Brand to act on (from distribute_status). Selects the organization holding it. Required when your key reaches several organizations, unless orgId is given.

orgId.description: Organization to act in (from distribute_status). Add it when a brand sits in several organizations, or to act in an organization without naming a brand.
